title: Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial of a Psychoeducational Add-On Intervention for Identifying and Discussing Negative Effects of Outpatient Psychotherapy in Children and Adolescents
summary:
Psychotherapy can help children and adolescents cope with mental health problems. However, unwanted or burdensome experiences and changes may also occur during psychotherapy. Such effects are not always discussed systematically during treatments. This study investigates an additional psychoeducational intervention. As part of this intervention, treating therapists use a workbook during a regularly scheduled psychotherapy session to inform patients about possible unwanted effects of psychotherapy. The therapist and patient then discuss whether such effects may have occurred during the patients' treatment. A total of 50 patients aged 11;00 to 18;11 years who are currently receiving outpatient psychotherapy are expected to participate in this study entitled "Discussing Negative Effects in Psychotherapy with Children and Adolescents“ (short: DisNEPsy). Participating patients will be randomly allocated to one of two groups. The first group receives the additional intervention at the beginning of the study. The second group receives it two weeks later and serves as a comparison group during the first two weeks. All participating patients continue their regular outpatient psychotherapy and receive the intervention.
Participation lasts four weeks. Questionnaires are completed at the beginning of the study, after two weeks and after four weeks. The study examines the relationship between patients and their therapists and patients' general self-efficacy. It also examines whether patients consider the intervention understandable, helpful and acceptable and whether therapists are able to deliver it as intended.
As the study is an exploratory study with 50 patients, its main purpose is to estimate potential effects and their uncertainty and to obtain information for planning a subsequent larger study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients' age between 11 years 0 months and 18 years 11 months at the time of enrollment
- Currently receiving outpatient psychotherapy in the Outpatient Psychotherapy Unit at the Department of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology and Psychotherapy at Trier University, Germany, with usually weekly scheduled therapy sessions
- The patient and treating therapist have completed at least 10 psychotherapy sessions together before study enrollment
- Written informed consent of the treating therapist
- Written informed consent of the patient
- From patients who are under 15 years of age: Additional written informed consent of the legal guardian(s) whose consent is required under the ethics approval and applicable legal requirements
Exclusion criteria:
There are no diagnosis-specific exclusion criteria regarding the type, duration, or severity of psychological symptoms. Concomitant pharmacotherapy is not an exclusion criterion. Patients will be excluded if, according to the clinical judgement of the treating therapist, there is a contraindication to the continuation of outpatient psychotherapy, particularly if the previous diagnostic findings or course of treatment indicate that more intensive treatment or a higher level of care is required.
